thread:
Nora Patel: FinSys Y just pushed back — security team wants clear artifact provenance + an emergency upgrade/rollback matrix before procurement signs off. They called out: SBOM, signing key storage, offline hotfix process, and whether we can apply model-only patches without full bundle replace.
Ethan Kim: TL;DR: artifacts are signed (ed25519) + manifest includes sbom url (for online) and embedded SBOM for sealed bundles. Key storage: we sign with Redwood KMS in-host when creating sealed bundles; customer can require signing by their HSM during handoff.
Ravi Desai: On the model-only patch ask: we support "model shard" delta patches in the installer. Flow for air-gapped sites:
1) Preinstall patcher/sidecar (part of initial bundle).
2) Deliver signed delta package on USB or via jumpbox.
3) Sidecar verifies signature (pubkey bundle that operator loaded) and applies in-place model swap with atomic symlink switch.
If swap fails we fallback to previous symlink and generate event.
Jules Martin: Does the atomic swap require service restart? Minimal restart — model process will restart gracefully (<30s) unless the customer disables graceful reload. We should document the exact KB to set to avoid POD restart in k8s.
Tess O'Connor: Security questionnaire note: they asked whether we can provide a deterministic verification procedure they can run offline. They want commands and checks: verify signature, verify sha256, verify SBOM hashes, and confirm timestamp. We'll need a one-page checklist in PDF for SOC.
ops-bot: Build: signed-sealed-bundle v2.0-poc sha256:ef12be34 staged /artifacts/sealed/4990001111; patcher image v0.8 built.
Ethan Kim: Upgrade cadence options we can propose: "Fast" monthly bundles with bugfix-only hotfix lane, "Stable" quarterly LTS, or "Enterprise" custom cadence with on-demand signed deltas. For FinSys Y POC recommend Fast + emergency delta support.
Nora Patel: Pricing question from procurement: price for emergency delta support (SLA <4h phone response) and cost to include customer HSM signing at handoff.
Jules Martin: Rough commercials: emergency delta support add-on $6k/month for POC (up to 3 incidents), HSM handoff one-time engineering runbook & key ceremony support $12k. Needs finance signoff.
Ravi Desai: Ops constraints to highlight in runbook: offline token exchange for automatic rollback requires a pre-provisioned admin token sealed in their vault; otherwise rollback is manual via USB signed manifest. Also mention the case where model binary ABI changes — that forces full bundle replace (can't hotpatch).
Tess O'Connor: Legal/SOW: we need explicit acceptance criteria for autonomous rollback, plus a clause that emergency patches applied by customer personnel are not covered under our SLA unless we are engaged for remote/onsite support. Will draft SOW snippet.
Nora Patel: Action items: @Ethan produce the one-page offline verification checklist and sample commands; @Ravi draft the rollback & model-patch runbook (CLI steps, USB verification, event IDs); @Jules send a preliminary quote for the emergency-delta add-on and HSM handoff fee. We'll coordinate SOC call once docs are ready.
Ethan Kim: I'll include examples like:
```
# verify signature
redwood-verify --pubkey /opt/redwood/pubkey.pem --file model-v2.delta --sig model-v2.delta.sig
# checksum
sha256sum model-v2.delta
```
Ravi Desai: I'll include k8s example and non-k8s systemd example; auto-rollback command will look like:
```
operatorctl rollback --node node-42 --bundle-id previous
```
Tess O'Connor: I'll start SOW snippet and ping legal for change-control language.
Nora Patel: Great — I'll update the customer with proposed cadence + pricing + ETA on docs (48h). If they still require 99.99% unattended recovery we should escalate to PS for a separate engineering engagement.
Jules Martin: Noted. Escalation path documented.
ops-bot: Note: telemetry opt-out flag respected in sealed bundles; audit logs are written to /var/log/redwood/audit.log when enabled.
Nora Patel: Perfect, I'll include that in the SOC Q&A. :thumbsup:
